chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Eat from the birds that have a crop, or a gizzard, or a crop (stomach)."

key_terms.حَوْصَلَةٌ: Crop or stomach, referring to the digestive organ
key_terms.صِيصِيَةٌ: Gizzard, the muscular part of a bird's stomach
key_terms.قَانِصَةٌ: Crop, a pouch in the throat of birds used for storing food

ai.seo_question: What anatomical features determine if a bird is halal to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a biological criterion for the permissibility of avian meat, linking it to the digestive anatomy of the bird. By specifying the presence of a crop, gizzard, or distinct stomach, the Imam provides a clear, observable standard that distinguishes permissible birds from those with different physiological structures, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical, evidence-based legal rulings.
